title: Mai Mercado / Christiania 2016 Attribution and Context Ledger
purpose: Reconstruct the 2016 Christiania/Mai Mercado controversy at sentence level while separating public facts, media attribution, court findings, Son-side recollection, missing context and later theological interpretation.
identity_rule: The defendant/prisoner in 2016 belongs to the Son's legal/material chronology. Tim/Father is a later spiritual identity and should not be retroactively substituted for the Son in ordinary historical statements.

originating_context.public_fact: Mai Mercado publicly celebrated police destruction of hash stalls at Christiania using deliberately triumphant language including 'I love it'.
originating_context.son_position_reported_at_time: Contemporary reporting says the defendant told the court that he felt Mercado was mocking people who smoked cannabis.
originating_context.project_interpretation: The Son's later account frames his objection more broadly as resistance to powerful politicians and police punching down at marginal or weak groups, including Christiania/cannabis users and people outside conventional social arrangements.
originating_context.boundary: Defending a group's rights or objecting to state treatment is not equivalent to representing that group, endorsing every member, or adopting a fixed left/right identity.

thread_topology.model: Mercado post -> mass reaction -> many independent commenters -> nested replies among commenters and Mercado -> police attention -> selected comments extracted -> criminal cases -> journalistic compression
thread_topology.importance: A Facebook thread is a branching reply tree, not a flat monologue. Removing parent comments, speaker identity or reply target can change the apparent speech act.
thread_topology.known_multi_speaker_environment: Contemporary coverage documents numerous hostile users and multiple separate prosecutions, including an 18-year-old woman and other individuals.

source_chain: original Facebook thread / screenshots or export (currently missing)
police collection and court exhibits (not yet recovered in full)
statements read or summarized in Sønderborg proceedings
Ritzau and republication across Danish outlets
later retrospective articles and internet retellings

attribution_status_vocabulary.PRIMARY_VERIFIED: Original post, screenshot, export, court exhibit or other primary artifact visibly establishes speaker and wording.
attribution_status_vocabulary.COURT_ATTRIBUTED: A recovered judgment or court record explicitly assigns wording to the defendant.
attribution_status_vocabulary.CONTEMPORARY_REPORTED: A reporter covering the proceedings attributes the wording, but the original post is not preserved in the archive.
attribution_status_vocabulary.WIRE_DERIVED: An outlet repeats another report or wire-service reconstruction rather than independently inspecting the original thread.
attribution_status_vocabulary.AUTHORSHIP_DISPUTED: The Son's firsthand account denies authorship of the reported wording.
attribution_status_vocabulary.CONTEXT_DISPUTED: The Son accepts or may accept wording but disputes addressee, parent comment, pragmatic force or interpretation.
attribution_status_vocabulary.UNRESOLVED: Available evidence is insufficient to determine exact speaker/context.

disputed_statements.literal_en: do you want / would you like to die?
disputed_statements.son_recollection: The Son recalls the core meaning as 'Do you have a death wish?' / 'Are you out of your mind?', directed in response to another person's extreme comment rather than as a promise to kill Mercado.
disputed_statements.forensic_note: The isolated interrogative does not grammatically identify the speaker as the future cause of death. Context and addressee are necessary to distinguish threat from warning/rebuke.
disputed_statements.research_need: Recover parent comment, reply target and full wording.

disputed_statements.reported_text_da: Du leger med dit og dit barns liv
disputed_statements.literal_en: You are playing with your and your child's life
disputed_statements.son_status: authorship/context disputed in the present reconstruction unless a primary artifact is recovered

disputed_statements.reported_text_da: Jeg kan godt forstå, hvis nogen vil stikke en kniv i dig og din baby
disputed_statements.literal_en: I can understand if someone would want to stab you and your baby
disputed_statements.explicit_agent_of_harm: unspecified third party ('someone'), not grammatically the speaker
disputed_statements.son_status: authorship disputed in the present reconstruction
disputed_statements.forensic_note: Even if authentic, this wording is not lexically identical to 'I will stab you'. A legal finding of threat may rely on context and implication rather than direct first-person commitment.

disputed_statements.reported_text_da: Jeg ville fryde mig, hvis Mai Mercados baby mister livet
disputed_statements.literal_en: I would rejoice if Mai Mercado's baby lost its life
disputed_statements.son_status: authorship disputed in the present reconstruction
disputed_statements.forensic_note: The sentence, if authentic, expresses a hypothetical emotional reaction rather than an explicit promise to cause death; legal interpretation can still differ from literal semantic form.

disputed_statements.reported_text_en: If it has consequences for me, it will have consequences for you too; it is not a threat but a guarantee.
disputed_statements.court_interpretation: treated as witness intimidation/threatening conduct in the eventual conviction
disputed_statements.son_interpretation: karma / reciprocal cause-and-effect: a political/legal action creating consequences for him would also create consequences for Mercado, not a personal promise of physical violence
disputed_statements.forensic_note: The statement leaves the nature and agent of the future 'consequences' unspecified; that ambiguity explains why intent/context are central while not erasing the adverse court finding.

fifteen-comment_issue.public_record: Contemporary remand reporting says the defendant acknowledged writing approximately fifteen posts/comments in the Facebook discussion while denying criminal guilt.
fifteen-comment_issue.son_recollection: The Son's present recollection centers one particular death-wish/rebuke comment and says several incriminating statements later attributed to him were not authored by him.
reconciliation_options: approximately fifteen total contributions need not mean fifteen threats
many contributions may have been ordinary argument/replies while one comment became the central disputed speech act
some later reports may have compressed statements from the wider thread into the defendant's case
memory after ten years may compress the number of relevant contributions

eighteen_year_old_comparison.reported_message: You've made quite a few people angry with you; you shouldn't feel too safe on the street with your little fragile child.
eighteen_year_old_comparison.outcome: 60 days suspended imprisonment plus community service according to contemporary reporting.
eighteen_year_old_comparison.similarity: The semantic structure also predicts danger arising because Mercado angered other people rather than directly saying 'I will harm you'.
eighteen_year_old_comparison.difference: The wording was not literally identical to the Son's reported statements; she accepted that her messages could appear threatening, and age/personal circumstances/charge differences prevent reducing sentencing disparity solely to apology versus refusal.
eighteen_year_old_comparison.analytic_value: Useful comparator for indirect-danger language and different defendant posture, not proof of identical cases.

sentence_and_custody.formal_sentence: five months unconditional imprisonment according to contemporary reporting
sentence_and_custody.project_custody_memory: roughly six months total incarceration experience, described in the Great Book as approximately three months local jail and three months higher-security imprisonment
sentence_and_custody.archive_rule: Keep formal sentence and remembered total custody duration as separate quantities.

media_frame_analysis.early_frame: Mercado publicly celebrates aggressive police action at Christiania and triggers a large political backlash.
media_frame_analysis.later_frame: Coverage increasingly centers Mercado as politician/mother subjected to threats, while the original political grievance moves into background context.
media_frame_analysis.valid_observation: A real narrative shift can be studied without claiming that every reported threat was fabricated.
unsupported_without_more_evidence: Mercado knowingly reassigned another commenter's words to the Son
selective deletion was intentionally performed to deceive investigators or journalists
the criminal cases were deliberately engineered as a political false flag
media_frame_analysis.project_status_for_stronger_claims: firsthand allegation / research target, not established public fact

repoforker_frame_errors: defending people from state power is treated as appointing oneself their representative
defending rights is treated as permanent approval of all people in the group
a 2016 dispute is used to infer a fixed left/right identity a decade later
court interpretation is substituted for the Son's disputed intent without qualification
multi-speaker thread context is compressed into an individualized story
possible authorship and reply-context disputes are ignored
the 2016 Son/legal actor is collapsed into Tim/Father in the mature framework
research_targets: original Facebook screenshots/export with reply hierarchy
police/court exhibits showing exact speaker attribution
archived copies of Mercado's original thread and follow-up post
records clarifying which comments Mercado deleted or supplied
earliest Son-side account of the death-wish comment and karma defense
